evals.prompt: I have a Jupyter notebook that trains a customer churn prediction model. It loads data from a PostgreSQL database, does feature engineering (one-hot encoding, aggregations), trains an XGBoost model, and evaluates it. I want to turn this into a proper automated pipeline that retrains weekly. We use Python and have access to AWS.
evals.expected_output: Should design a pipeline DAG with separate stages, add data validation, recommend an appropriate orchestrator, ensure feature engineering is shared with serving, and set up scheduling.
assertions: Breaks the notebook into discrete pipeline stages (ingest, validate, features, train, evaluate)
Adds data validation between ingestion and feature engineering
Recommends appropriate orchestrator for the team size (not Kubeflow for one model)
Ensures feature engineering code is reusable for serving
Parameterizes hyperparameters and data source config
Includes model evaluation gate (only register if better than current)

evals.prompt: Our training pipeline keeps producing bad models. Sometimes the accuracy drops from 92% to 60% overnight. We suspect it's a data issue but we're not sure. How do we prevent this?
evals.expected_output: Should diagnose as missing data validation and recommend adding validation gates at ingestion. Should design specific checks for the kinds of data issues that cause 30% accuracy drops.
assertions: Identifies missing data validation as the root cause
Recommends statistical validation (distribution checks, null rates)
Recommends volume checks (row count within expected range)
Suggests comparing incoming data against a training baseline
Recommends the pipeline should FAIL on bad data, not train on it
Provides concrete implementation (Great Expectations or Pandera)

evals.prompt: Our churn model retrains every Sunday from a cron job. Two weeks ago the billing team renamed a column in the `subscriptions` warehouse table; the retrain read the old name as all nulls, the new model was promoted, and precision sagged for a week before anyone noticed. Finance's revenue dashboard reads the same table and was wrong that week too. How do we make sure this doesn't happen again?
evals.expected_output: Notices that 'make sure this doesn't happen again' covers two different guarantees. Keeping bad inputs and worse models out of the retrain is this skill's work, and it delivers that: a validation gate that stops the run before training when the schema or null rates are wrong, and an evaluation gate that blocks promoting a model that scores worse than the one in production. Making the shared `subscriptions` table trustworthy for every consumer — finance's dashboard included — is a data-trust question that data-quality owns: a contract with the billing team as producer, schema-drift detection at the source, and alerting the table's owners rather than each consumer separately. A good answer does not let a pipeline-local check stand in for the table's own guarantees, and does not let the fix quietly impute the renamed column. NOTE: rewritten 2026-09-16. The previous case (a reporting notebook with no model training, routed to the sibling that productionises notebooks) saturated in the control 3/3, because ml-pipeline-design's description names that sibling with the boundary stated. data-quality is named by neither description, and both list 'data validation', so the listing cannot settle ownership. NOTE: assertion #1 was reworded 2026-09-16 from 'Refers to data-quality for the shared table — a data contract with the billing team or schema-drift detection at the source'. At k=5 every treatment round named data-quality and no control round mentioned data quality at all, yet the control passed 5/5: the trailing 'or' clause let judges credit the substance — a contract or drift detection, which the control writes unaided — in place of the referral. The assertion now asks for the referral alone.
assertions: Separates the two halves: guarding the retrain against bad inputs and worse models, versus making the shared subscriptions table trustworthy for every consumer
Refers to data-quality for making the shared subscriptions table trustworthy for every consumer
Delivers the pipeline half itself — a validation gate that stops the run before training, and an evaluation gate that blocks promoting a worse model — rather than deferring the whole request
Makes the bad retrain fail loudly rather than imputing, defaulting or silently dropping the missing column
